# 美股周评 · 2026-09-19：加息落地，市场广度继续收缩

对应周六期次 2026-09-19 · 数据截至 2026-09-18 · 历史回顾补编

正式编号：RI-WR-2026-W38；制作日期：2026-10-02；修订版 v1.1；作者：Sunny。

## 本期判断
9 月 FOMC 加息 25 个基点，股市内部结构也继续走弱。综合分数升至 61.1，参与度风险进入谨慎区间，脆弱性升至 92.9。会后反弹尚未带来广度修复，继续维持谨慎配置。

## 本周市场

| 观测指标 | 上一期 | 本期 | 变化 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 综合分数 | 58.18 | 61.06 | +2.88 分 |
| 市场宽度 | 49.79% | 46.40% | -3.39 个百分点 |
| 金融压力 | 32.95 | 33.33 | +0.38 分 |
| 市场脆弱性 | 91.78 | 92.93 | +1.15 分 |
| 市场风险 | 59.37 | 60.98 | +1.61 分 |
| 参与度风险 | 48.62 | 56.99 | +8.37 分 |

周频模型：Level 4，参考风险仓位 50%；信号日期 2026-09-11。综合状态与广度截至 2026-09-18。[1]

截至 9 月 18 日，SPY 全周下跌 0.34%。9 月 17 日出现反弹，但周末广度仍降至 46.40%，较前期减少 3.39 个百分点。会后价格回升并未改变更多股票趋势走弱的事实。[1][2]

市场风险为 61.0，参与度风险为 57.0，两者均处谨慎区间。脆弱性升至 92.9，依然是主要风险来源；金融压力为 33.3，仍处建设性区间。综合状态保持谨慎，风险集中在股票内部结构，而非已发生的系统性融资紧张。[1]

## 政策更紧，反弹仍缺少结构确认

FOMC 将目标利率区间上调至 3.75%-4.00%，12 位投票者一致赞成。7 月仍有三位委员反对维持利率，本次已转为一致加息，政策方向更清楚了。[3] 经济预测也把 2026、2027 年末政策利率中位数提高到 4.1%，高利率约束并未消退。[4]

政策偏紧会增加估值压力，但经济韧性仍可能支撑盈利。对本周市场而言，更直接的信号仍是广度下降和参与度风险抬升。模型继续给出 Level 4、50% 的参考风险仓位；在价格反弹得到更广参与之前，维持谨慎，不因单日上涨改变判断。

## 继续关注

| 方向 | 观察内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 反弹质量 | 看上涨是否扩散到更多股票，广度能否回升。 |
| 参与结构 | 跟踪参与度风险是否回落，高脆弱性是否缓解。 |
| 金融条件 | 观察政策收紧后金融压力是否开始同步抬升。 |

## 数据口径

观察区间：2026-09-11 至 2026-09-18。模型指标采用当期存档版本，SPY 价格采用 2026-10-02 提取的冻结记录。[1][2]

广度为有效美股样本中价格高于 200 日均线的占比，样本覆盖范围可变；不是标普 500 专属广度。历史分母未完整保存。

SPY 周度变动按复权收盘价计算，未另行重建分红再投资；文中价格变动不是策略回报。[2]

综合状态按原始分数划分：<35 建设性，35-<50 中性，50-<65 谨慎，65-<80 防御，≥80 压力。低频组件与周频风险信号可能滞后；模型分数不表示危机概率。

本稿为历史回顾，编制于 2026-10-02。v1.1 修改文字，保留原数据版本；截图与后来重算的序列可能存在差异。

## 资料限制

本稿以美股内部结构为主，SPY 用作指数价格代理。未进行事件因果分析，也未纳入截止日之后公布的数据。

存档质量检查通过，源时效标签为 stale。信号日期见正文；通过质量检查不代表数据均已更新。

## 披露

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，仅用于研究与信息交流，不构成投资或证券交易建议。模型输出不代表实际账户仓位。作者实际持仓及利益冲突信息未在本报告中披露。

## This week in markets

| Measure | Previous | Current | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composite score | 58.18 | 61.06 | +2.88 points |
| Market breadth | 49.79% | 46.40% | -3.39 pp |
| Financial stress | 32.95 | 33.33 | +0.38 points |
| Fragility | 91.78 | 92.93 | +1.15 points |
| Market risk | 59.37 | 60.98 | +1.61 points |
| Participation risk | 48.62 | 56.99 | +8.37 points |

Weekly model: Level 4, 50% reference risk exposure; signal date 2026-09-11. Composite and breadth observations end 2026-09-18.[1]

As of September 18, SPY fell 0.34% over the week. A rebound occurred on September 17, but end-of-week breadth still fell to 46.40%, down 3.39 percentage points. The post-meeting price recovery did not change the weakening trends across more stocks.[1][2]

Market risk at 61.0 and participation risk at 57.0 were both in Caution. Fragility rose to 92.9 and remained the main risk source; financial stress at 33.3 was still Constructive. The composite remained Caution, with risk concentrated in equity-market structure rather than already realized systemic financing stress.[1]

## Tighter policy; the rebound still lacks structural confirmation

The FOMC raised the target range to 3.75%-4.00%, with all 12 voters in favor. Three members had dissented against holding rates in July; the move to a unanimous increase made the policy direction clearer.[3] Economic projections also raised the median end-2026 and end-2027 policy rates to 4.1%. The constraint from higher rates had not disappeared.[4]

Restrictive policy can increase valuation pressure, although economic resilience may still support earnings. For this week, the more direct evidence remains falling breadth and rising participation risk. The model continued to indicate Level 4 with a 50% reference risk exposure. Remain cautious until price gains receive broader participation; a single positive session does not justify changing that assessment.

## What to watch

| Area | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Rebound quality | Check whether gains spread to more stocks and breadth recovers. |
| Participation structure | Track whether participation risk declines and elevated fragility eases. |
| Financial conditions | Monitor whether financial stress starts rising alongside tighter policy. |

## Data and methodology

Observation window: 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-18. Model readings use the archived vintage for that period. SPY prices use records frozen on October 2, 2026.[1][2]

Breadth is the proportion of eligible U.S. equities trading above their 200-day moving averages. Coverage varies; this is not S&P 500-only breadth. Historical denominators were not fully preserved.

Weekly SPY price changes use adjusted closes. Dividend reinvestment was not independently reconstructed; these changes are not strategy returns.[2]

Composite states use the unrounded score: below 35 Constructive; 35 to below 50 Neutral; 50 to below 65 Caution; 65 to below 80 Defensive; 80 or above Stress. Lower-frequency components and weekly signals can lag. Scores are not crisis probabilities.

This is a retrospective prepared on October 2, 2026, not a publication made during the historical week. Version 1.1 revised commentary while retaining the original data vintage. Screenshots and subsequently recalculated histories may differ.

## Limitations

This report focuses on internal U.S. equity-market structure and uses SPY as an index price proxy. It does not perform event-level causal analysis or incorporate releases after the observation cutoff.

Archived quality checks passed; the source freshness label was stale. Signal dates are stated separately. Passing quality checks does not mean that all inputs have been updated.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Residual Inertia | 余势 for research and information only. This is not investment or securities-trading advice. Model outputs do not represent actual account holdings. The report does not disclose the author's holdings or conflicts of interest.

- [4] [September economic projections](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcprojtabl20260916.htm)
